summary:
What if the next discovery in astronomy began with someone who isn't a scientist?

EUREKA – Open Astronomy is an interactive citizen-science platform developed by AstroTwins to make real astronomical research accessible to everyone, regardless of scientific background.

Using NASA's astronomical archives, including NEOWISE and SPHEREx observations, EUREKA allows users to explore an interactive sky map, examine real images, investigate the apparent motion of celestial objects, and document their findings.

We demonstrated its scientific capabilities by analyzing nine NEOWISE images of the known asteroid 128 Nemesis, measuring four astrometric positions, and comparing our results with NASA JPL Horizons predictions, with a maximum reported deviation of approximately 0.51 arcseconds.

Our vision is to connect citizens and researchers through a future open discovery network, where scientifically reviewed observations could contribute to astronomical research and potentially support planetary defense.

Because curiosity should be the only prerequisite for exploring the Universe.
details:
EUREKA — Open Astronomy

Developed by AstroTwins | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. The Challenge, Our Motivation and Our Vision

What if the next discovery in astronomy began with someone who isn't a scientist?

This question inspired EUREKA.

We live in an era of unprecedented access to astronomical observations. NASA missions continuously expand our understanding of the Universe, producing vast amounts of publicly available scientific data. Yet, despite this openness, exploring and interpreting these observations often requires specialized knowledge, technical experience, and familiarity with astronomical software.

At the same time, increasingly automated scientific analysis raises a question that motivated our team: how can we preserve people's active involvement in the process of discovery?

We created EUREKA – Open Astronomy, an interactive citizen-science platform designed to bridge the gap between the public and astronomical research.

Our mission is not simply to make scientific information understandable, but to make the scientific process itself accessible. We want people to observe, investigate, measure, question, and evaluate real astronomical evidence, regardless of their scientific background.

EUREKA addresses the Planet X & SPHEREx challenge by allowing users to investigate how the sky changes over time through authentic astronomical observations.

2. How EUREKA Works

EUREKA transforms complex astronomical archives into an accessible, interactive exploration experience.

Users begin by navigating a celestial map, where they can pan, zoom, and select a region of the sky. Their selection is translated into celestial coordinates — Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) — which guide searches for available observations in NASA's astronomical archives.

Through NASA/IPAC IRSA, the platform works with real observational datasets associated with missions including WISE, NEOWISE, and SPHEREx.

Users can examine astronomical images obtained at different times, compare observations, inspect timestamps, investigate apparent motion, and evaluate possible moving celestial objects.

The platform also includes a Candidate Scanner, designed to support preliminary screening of potentially moving sources, alongside tools for examining candidate evidence and checking possible identifications.

Rather than automatically declaring discoveries, EUREKA encourages users to examine the evidence and distinguish known objects from candidates requiring further investigation.

An interactive guide and video tutorial provide step-by-step assistance, enabling students, amateur astronomers, and people without previous scientific experience to engage with real astronomical data.

The platform requires no personal telescope or specialized observational equipment.

3. Scientific Validation — Asteroid 128 Nemesis

An essential part of our project was demonstrating that EUREKA could support meaningful astronomical measurements rather than simply display images.

To evaluate our observational workflow, we selected the known asteroid 128 Nemesis as a scientific validation case.

We analyzed nine real NEOWISE W2 images spanning approximately 20.41 hours, obtaining four astrometric positions over 17.26 hours.

Using astronomical FITS data and World Coordinate System (WCS) information, we determined the asteroid's celestial coordinates and investigated its apparent motion across successive observations.

We independently compared our measured positions with orbital ephemerides from NASA JPL Horizons.

The maximum reported positional deviation was approximately 0.51 arcseconds, supporting the successful identification of the known asteroid.

This validation demonstrates the potential of our approach to investigate real celestial motion using archival observations and independently predicted positions.

Importantly, this was a successful identification of an already known object, not a claim of discovering a new asteroid. This distinction reflects our commitment to scientific accuracy and responsible interpretation.

4. Technology, Tools and Development

EUREKA combines web development technologies with genuine scientific data services.

Frontend Development

  • HTML and CSS for the platform's structure, visual identity, and user interface.
  • JavaScript for interactive functionality, astronomical observations, and celestial navigation.
  • D3-Celestial for sky mapping based on astronomical reference coordinates.

Backend and Scientific Data

  • Node.js for server-side operations and communication with astronomical data services.
  • NASA/IPAC IRSA for accessing observational archives, including WISE, NEOWISE, and SPHEREx datasets.
  • FITS files and WCS information for astronomical image analysis and coordinate interpretation.
  • NASA JPL Horizons for independent comparison with predicted celestial positions.

Scientific Functionality

  • Candidate Scanner for preliminary investigation of potentially moving sources.
  • Observation comparison, motion assessment, identification checks, and evidence documentation.

Development and Deployment

  • GitHub for source-code management.
  • Render for online deployment and public access.

The platform is web-based and can be accessed through a standard browser, without requiring users to install specialized astronomical software.

5. What Makes EUREKA Creative and Different?

EUREKA is built around a simple but powerful principle:

Scientific discovery should be something people can participate in, not merely something they read about.

Unlike conventional astronomy platforms that primarily present celestial images or established scientific results, EUREKA invites users to investigate authentic observations and engage directly with the reasoning behind astronomical discoveries.

Its originality lies in combining several elements within a single accessible environment:

  • Real NASA observations: Users examine genuine scientific data rather than simulations or purely illustrative images.
  • Hands-on investigation: The platform encourages measurement, comparison, and critical evaluation instead of passive viewing.
  • Scientific verification: Candidate observations can be assessed using astronomical coordinates, observation times, and independent reference information.
  • Accessibility: An intuitive interface, interactive sky map, and guided learning experience make advanced astronomical data approachable to non-specialists.
  • Citizen-science potential: Documented observations could eventually become a starting point for collaboration with professional researchers.

Throughout development, we considered scientific reliability, observational provenance, data quality, possible false positives, ease of use, and the importance of distinguishing preliminary evidence from confirmed astronomical discoveries.

Our goal was to balance accessibility with scientific responsibility, allowing users to explore freely without compromising the credibility of their findings.

6. Intended Impact — The EUREKA Discovery Network

Our vision extends beyond individual exploration.

The next stage of EUREKA is the proposed EUREKA Discovery Network, a future framework designed to connect citizen observations with the scientific community.

Under this proposed system, interesting observations could be organized into structured evidence packages containing astronomical images, celestial coordinates, observation timestamps, and supporting measurements.

Following independent scientific review, suitable candidate reports could become accessible through a public, searchable archive.

Selected verified datasets could also be published through repositories such as Zenodo, with persistent Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs), allowing researchers to access and reference them.

Future extensions could include notifications connecting relevant findings with interested scientists.

These capabilities represent our development roadmap. The public candidate archive, automated scientific submissions, and researcher notification network are not yet operational.

7. Potential Contributions to Planetary Defense

One particularly meaningful long-term application of EUREKA concerns the observation of small Solar System bodies.

With appropriate validation and professional scientific oversight, suitable astrometric measurements could potentially contribute to follow-up investigations and established reporting processes, including submissions to the Minor Planet Center (MPC).

Such information may support the identification and orbital characterization of small bodies, providing an indirect connection to the broader scientific efforts associated with planetary defense.

Organizations such as NASA JPL's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) and NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office (PDCO) demonstrate the importance of accurate observations and orbital knowledge.

EUREKA does not currently submit observations automatically to these organizations, predict asteroid impacts, or maintain institutional collaborations with them. These references describe potential scientific pathways for future development.

8. Our Mission — Bringing People and Science Together

Ultimately, EUREKA is about more than astronomy or technology.

It is about curiosity, scientific literacy, critical thinking, and the belief that meaningful engagement with science should not be limited to professional researchers.

By transforming publicly available NASA observations into an interactive environment for exploration and investigation, we aim to encourage more people to understand how scientific knowledge is produced and to develop the confidence to ask their own questions.

Our long-term ambition is to build a bridge between curious minds and the scientific community, where carefully documented observations could one day support genuine research.

Perhaps the next discovery will not be a new celestial object.

Perhaps it will be a person discovering, for the first time, the excitement of participating in science.

We do not simply want to show people the Universe. We want to give them the opportunity to help explore it.

Curiosity drives discovery.
